::: {.lead}
Today you use an AI assistant for real jobs, and you check its answers with
other tools: Word, a spreadsheet and the university website. Each
experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in the app on a computer. **Part B**
is on your phone or on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper,
scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write
your result in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a computer with a browser, Word and Excel (the desktop
  apps, or Word and Excel on the web at `office.com`), an AI assistant that
  the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your
  university account), a search engine (`bing.com`), and your phone.
- **No lab computer today?** Your teacher does Part A on the screen, on the
  simulators of the interactive lesson and in an AI assistant. Do Part B on
  your phone.
- **The prompts:** on the interactive lesson, each prompt has a **Copy
  prompt** button. On paper, type it exactly as it is printed.
- **Never type personal data** (your ID number, phone or address) into the
  AI assistant.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · A first draft, checked

**The idea:** an AI assistant learned from a huge amount of text: its
**training data**. It writes likely words, so it is fast, but likely is not
always true, and the same prompt can give a different answer. Five good
jobs for AI: a **draft**, a **summary**, **ideas**, a **rewrite** and a
**translation**. You read and check every answer before you use it.

**Aim:** get a first draft from an AI assistant, and correct it.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Copy this prompt into the AI assistant. Paste its draft into a new Word
   document with **Keep Text Only** (Paste Options). Read it line by line,
   delete every fact that is **not** in the prompt, and make the title
   **bold**.

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write a short notice for the students of our college. The college
   library has new opening hours from Sunday 15 November: 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.,
   Sunday to Thursday. Students can borrow three books for two weeks. Use a
   title and three short lines.
   :::

   {{< record "A fact that I deleted (or: none)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good draft keeps every fact of the prompt: from Sunday 15 November,
   8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Sunday to Thursday, three books for two weeks. Often
   it adds **nothing**, but a draft may add a fact, for example "Coffee is
   free in the reading room" or "The library opens on Saturday". Delete it:
   you are responsible for the text that you use.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   A draft has five lines. Which are in the prompt, and which did the AI add?

   In the prompt: keep it
   :   The library opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 4 p.m.

       Why: These are the hours of the prompt.

   :   Students can borrow three books for two weeks.

       Why: The prompt says three books for two weeks.

   :   The new hours start on Sunday 15 November.

       Why: The date is in the prompt.

   Added by the AI: delete it
   :   The library is also open on Saturday.

       Why: The prompt says Sunday to Thursday only.

   :   Coffee is free in the reading room.

       Why: The prompt says nothing about coffee: the AI added it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On your phone** (an AI app, or its website)
:::

2. On your phone, open an AI assistant (the Copilot app, or
   `copilot.microsoft.com`), start a **new chat** and send the same prompt
   again. Is the second draft the same as the first?

   {{< record "Same or different? One difference" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Different:** other words, maybe another title. The AI writes likely
   words, not always the same ones. The facts must still be right: check
   them again.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You send the same prompt in a new chat. Why is the second draft different?

   - [x] The AI writes likely words, not always the same ones.

     Why: The same prompt can give another answer, so you check each answer.

   - [ ] The first draft was wrong.

     Why: Both drafts can be good; they are only in other words.

   - [ ] The phone has a smaller AI.

     Why: The device does not matter: the same AI writes other likely words.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Check the numbers

**The idea:** AI answers have five weak spots. **Invented facts:** a book, a
name or a link that does not exist (a **hallucination**). **Old
information:** the AI learned from data up to a date, its **knowledge
cutoff**. **Wrong numbers** in sums and percentages. **Bias:** unfair ideas
from its data. **Missing context:** it does not know your class, job or
company. For exact numbers, use a spreadsheet.

**Aim:** catch a wrong number with a spreadsheet.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant and Excel)**
:::

1. Copy this prompt into the AI assistant. Check its total in Excel: type
   the table, then **=B2\*C2** in D2, copied to D3, and **=SUM(D2:D3)** in
   D4. (No Excel? **Bill Check** on the interactive lesson.)

   ::: {.prompt}
   A class buys 12 pens at 0.25 JD each and 5 notebooks at 1.20 JD each.
   What is the total price?
   :::

   | | A | B | C | D |
   |:-:|---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | Item | Price (JD) | Quantity | Total (JD) |
   | 2 | Pen | 0.25 | 12 | |
   | 3 | Notebook | 1.20 | 5 | |
   | 4 | All | | | |

   {{< record "AI … JD; Excel … JD" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Excel gives **9.00 JD** (3.00 + 6.00). Many AI answers are right here,
   but some give another number, and they sound just as sure. For exact
   numbers, use a spreadsheet: a wrong number is a weak spot of AI.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="9|9.00|9.0" unit="JD" hint="12 × 0.25 in D2, 5 × 1.20 in D3, then add them."}
   What does =SUM(D2:D3) give for the class's bill?

   Why: 12 × 0.25 = 3.00 JD and 5 × 1.20 = 6.00 JD: 9.00 JD in all.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/weak-spots.html" poster="sims/weak-spots.png" title="Weak Spots: what is wrong with this AI answer?" >}}

2. In **Weak Spots**, read each AI answer and the line "What you know", and
   choose its weak spot. Do all seven answers.

   {{< record "My score … of 7" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The seven answers: two invented facts (a book, an award), old
   information (an app version), a wrong number (12 pens), bias (the nurse
   is "she"), missing context (the homework topic) and one good draft.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   One of the seven answers in Weak Spots has no weak spot. Which one?

   - [x] three tips for a polite e-mail: a clear subject, a greeting, a thank-you

     Why: Normal, useful tips: a good job for AI. Read it, and use your own words.

   - [ ] Sunrise Company won Best Shop in Amman in 2024.

     Why: The company records show no award: an invented fact.

   - [ ] Dear teacher, here is my homework about the history of Rome…

     Why: Missing context: the homework is about Excel charts.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · The right tool

**The idea:** choose the tool by the job. An **AI assistant** for drafts,
summaries, ideas and translations. A **search engine** (Bing, Google) for
today's facts, dates, rules and prices: it finds web pages, and you read
the real source, for example the university website. A **spreadsheet**
(Excel) for exact numbers. With AI, follow five steps: **ask, read, check,
edit, use**.

**Aim:** compare an AI answer with the real source.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant and the university website)**
:::

1. Copy this prompt into the AI assistant. Then open the website of the
   university and look for the library or its opening hours. Which answer
   do you trust?

   ::: {.prompt}
   What are the opening hours of the library of Al-Israa University in
   Amman?
   :::

   {{< record "The AI says … ; I trust … , because …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI may give hours from an old page, or invent them, and it sounds
   sure either way. A good answer: "I trust the university website. It is
   the official source, and it is up to date." If the website does not show
   the hours, the next source is the library itself (a phone call or the
   notice at the door), not the AI.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI and the university website give different hours. Which do you trust?

   - [x] the university website

     Why: It is the official source, and it is up to date. If it does not show the hours, ask the library itself.

   - [ ] the AI, because it answers faster

     Why: Fast is not true: the AI may use an old page.

   - [ ] the AI, if it gives a link

     Why: A link in an AI answer is not proof: open it and read the page.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/right-tool.html" poster="sims/right-tool.png" title="Right Tool: AI, search or spreadsheet?" >}}

2. Play **Right Tool**. Then write the tool for each job: the last day to
   pay the fees, the total of 40 prices, a polite reminder e-mail.

   {{< record "Fees … ; 40 prices … ; e-mail …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **A search engine** and the official university website (dates and
   rules), **a spreadsheet** (it adds exactly), **an AI assistant** (a
   draft that you read and change).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which tool fits each job? Sort them.

   A search engine
   :   the last day to pay the fees

       Why: Dates and rules: find them on the official university website.

   A spreadsheet
   :   the total of 40 prices

       Why: A spreadsheet adds exactly.

   An AI assistant
   :   a polite reminder e-mail

       Why: A draft that you read and change.
   :::
